summary: This article explains how your eyes see, why long screen time can leave them tired and dry, and simple habits like the 20-20-20 rule and outdoor play that protect them.
introduce: Write “Problem” and “Solution” on the board and give pairs thirty seconds to think of a problem people face in daily life and one way to fix it. Explain that as they read “Eyes and Screens”, they will look for the main problem and how it is solved.

keyTerms.def: the small black opening in the center of the eye that lets light in
the thin layer at the back of the eye that changes light into signals for the brain
a part of the body that tightens and relaxes to make something move

challengeTerms.def: related to the eye or to seeing
the medical word for being nearsighted
a feeling of being very tired

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that kids should have a time limit for using screens every day? Use evidence from the article to explain.
struggling: Pre-teach pupil, retina, and muscle with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers fill in a simple Problem | Solution chart with sentence starters.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use optic, myopia, and fatigue in a short paragraph that suggests a second solution to the problem and judge which works better.
